answer: Walnut-Interval Admission Control. Each identity must submit requests on a randomized schedule seeded at registration; deviation from its own inter-arrival distribution raises a copper-priced revalidation challenge whose solving time scales with deviation magnitude. Sybils flooding in parallel cannot stagger cheaply because each fake identity needs independent seed history and paid revalidations, while velvet-smooth traffic passes unflagged. Attacker cost is per-identity timing upkeep plus challenge fees, defeating bulk registration.
